solution_principle:
3- Lists: Wrapping

- Wrapping means that the List starts again at the end without stopping.

- The below List has 10 items, first index is 0 and last index is 9.

- Try to choose the 10th index with the "List Item" component.

- The "List Item" component has a BOOLEAN INPUT "W".

- In Grasshopper, BOOLEAN does not mean geometry merge as in other software, it rather means "true" or "false".

- In this case, let us see what happens when we choose the item with 10th idex (which does not exist since the last item has the index 9).

- With a "True" BOOLEAN, the List seems to loop and start again from the beginning, hence the 10th item is 1.

- With a "False" BOOLEAN, the List gives a "null" result. In other words, it is saying that there is no 10th item to be displayed.

3- Lists: Wrapping

- Wrapping means that the List starts again at the end without stopping.

- The below List has 10 items, first index is 0 and last index is 9.

- In this case, let us see what happens when we choose the item with 10th idex (which does not exist since the last item has the index 9).

- With a "True" BOOLEAN, the List seems to loop and start again from the beginning, hence the 10th item is 1.

- With a "False" BOOLEAN, the List gives a "null" result. In other words, it is saying that there is no 10th item to be displayed.
